title: Mock 4 · Valuation Warm-up
blurb: A relative-valuation caselet, working-capital and leverage ratios, buyback maths, report quality and the RA code of conduct.

questions.q: Which quality is most important for a research analyst when management presents a very optimistic growth outlook?
options: Accepting management guidance as the base case
Professional scepticism - testing claims against data and independent checks
Matching the consensus view to avoid standing out
questions.explanation: Analysts should listen to management but verify claims with data, channel checks and history. Independence and scepticism are core qualities.
hints: Uncritical acceptance defeats the purpose of research.
Meeting management is a legitimate and useful activity.
Herding with consensus is not independent analysis.

questions.q: Participatory notes (P-notes) are:
options: Promissory notes issued by the RBI
Short-term bonds issued by Indian companies abroad
Notes issued by SEBI to registered intermediaries
Offshore derivative instruments issued by registered FPIs to overseas investors, with Indian securities as the underlying
questions.explanation: P-notes (ODIs) let overseas investors gain exposure to Indian securities through a registered FPI without registering themselves.
hints: SEBI does not issue such notes.

questions.q: If market interest rates (yields) rise, the price of an existing fixed-coupon bond will generally:
options: Rise only if it is a zero-coupon bond
questions.explanation: Bond prices move inversely to yields: higher yields reduce the present value of fixed coupons and principal.
hints: This is the opposite of the inverse relationship.
Market prices change daily with yields.
Zero-coupon bonds fall even more (higher duration).

questions.q: Building a multi-factor model that screens stocks on value, momentum and quality using historical data is an example of:
questions.explanation: Quantitative analysis applies statistical and econometric models to large datasets to identify relationships and select securities.
hints: Technical analysis focuses on price/volume charts.

questions.q: Under India's flexible inflation targeting framework, RBI's target for CPI inflation is:
questions.explanation: The target is 4% CPI inflation with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%.
hints: 6% is the upper tolerance limit, not the target.
The target is on CPI, not WPI.

questions.q: In industry analysis, 'SCP' stands for:
questions.explanation: The SCP paradigm holds that market structure influences firm conduct, which in turn determines industry performance.

questions.q: After the abolition of Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) from 1 April 2020, dividends received from Indian companies are:
options: Taxed only at the company level
Taxed in the hands of the shareholders
questions.explanation: With DDT removed, companies pay dividends without DDT and shareholders are taxed on dividend income under the applicable rules.
hints: Dividends are not exempt after DDT removal.
Company-level dividend tax (DDT) was what was abolished.
STT applies to securities transactions, not dividends.

questions.q: A company's credit rating has been downgraded twice in 18 months and is now on 'watch with negative implications'. An equity analyst should read this as:
options: A sign of deteriorating financial strength that needs closer scrutiny
A guaranteed default within a year
A signal to raise the target price
questions.explanation: Tracking rating history helps detect weakening finances early. Successive downgrades and a negative watch call for a close look at leverage, liquidity and cash flows.
hints: Credit stress directly affects equity value.
Ratings indicate probability, not certainty, of default.
It is a negative signal, not a positive one.

questions.q: A company has trade receivables of ₹150 crore and annual sales of ₹1,095 crore. Its receivable days (365-day year) are:
questions.explanation: Receivable days = receivables / sales x 365 = 150 / 1,095 x 365 = 50 days.

questions.q: A company has total debt of ₹600 crore and shareholders' equity of ₹1,500 crore. Its debt-equity ratio is:
A 'qualified opinion' in an auditor's report means that:
options: The financial statements are true and fair in all respects
The auditor could not form any opinion
The statements are fair except for specific matters the auditor disagrees with or could not verify
questions.explanation: A qualified ('except for') opinion flags specific issues. An unqualified opinion is clean; an adverse opinion says statements are not fair; a disclaimer means no opinion could be formed.
hints: The term refers to the opinion, not the auditor's credentials.
That is a disclaimer of opinion.

questions.q: A company with PAT of ₹200 crore and 40 crore shares buys back 4 crore shares. Assuming PAT is unchanged, its EPS after the buyback is approximately:
questions.explanation: EPS before = 200/40 = ₹5.00. After buyback shares = 36 crore, EPS = 200/36 ≈ ₹5.56.
hints: This uses 44 crore shares (added instead of subtracted).
Simply adding 10% to EPS is not the right computation.

questions.q: Use the case data. Applying the peer EV/EBITDA multiple, the implied enterprise value of Neelgiri Foods is:
questions.explanation: Implied EV = 9 x ₹1,200 crore = ₹10,800 crore.
hints: This subtracts net debt from EV - that gives equity value, not EV.
questions.case: Neelgiri Foods Ltd: EBITDA ₹1,200 crore; total debt ₹2,000 crore; cash ₹400 crore; shares outstanding 40 crore; EPS ₹15. Listed peers trade at an average EV/EBITDA of 9x and an average P/E of 18x. An analyst is building a relative-valuation cross-check.

questions.q: Use the case data. Based on the EV/EBITDA method, the implied value per share is:
questions.explanation: Equity = EV - debt + cash = 10,800 - 2,000 + 400 = ₹9,200 crore; per share = 9,200 / 40 = ₹230.
hints: This divides EV by shares without the net-debt adjustment.
This subtracts debt but ignores cash.
This subtracts cash instead of adding it.
questions.case: Neelgiri Foods Ltd: EBITDA ₹1,200 crore; total debt ₹2,000 crore; cash ₹400 crore; shares outstanding 40 crore; EPS ₹15. Listed peers trade at an average EV/EBITDA of 9x and an average P/E of 18x. An analyst is building a relative-valuation cross-check.

questions.q: Use the case data. Based on the peer P/E multiple, the implied value per share is:
questions.explanation: Implied price = peer P/E x EPS = 18 x ₹15 = ₹270.
hints: This would need a P/E of 20x.
questions.case: Neelgiri Foods Ltd: EBITDA ₹1,200 crore; total debt ₹2,000 crore; cash ₹400 crore; shares outstanding 40 crore; EPS ₹15. Listed peers trade at an average EV/EBITDA of 9x and an average P/E of 18x. An analyst is building a relative-valuation cross-check.

questions.q: Weekly data show that global crude oil inventories have fallen much more than expected for several weeks. For crude prices, this is generally:
questions.explanation: Falling inventories indicate demand exceeding supply (a tighter market), which tends to support prices.
hints: Inventory build-ups, not draws, are bearish.
Inventory data are closely watched precisely because they move prices.
Crude inventory data relate to crude oil.

questions.q: A portfolio earned 16% with a beta of 1.25 when the risk-free rate was 6%. Its Treynor ratio is:
hints: This is 16/1.25 - ignores the risk-free rate.

questions.q: The risk that coupons received from a bond will have to be invested at lower interest rates than the bond's yield is called:
questions.explanation: Reinvestment risk arises when interim cash flows can only be reinvested at lower rates. Zero-coupon bonds have no reinvestment risk.
hints: Credit risk is the risk of default.
Liquidity risk is difficulty in selling at a fair price.
Call risk is the issuer redeeming early, usually when rates fall.

questions.q: Which of the following should NOT appear in a good research report?
options: A statement assuring readers that the target price is guaranteed
questions.explanation: Guaranteeing returns or targets is misleading and against the code of conduct. Risks, valuation basis and disclosures are hallmarks of a good report.
hints: The valuation basis should be stated.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the heads of the Code of Conduct for research analysts (Third Schedule)?
questions.explanation: The eight heads are honesty and good faith, diligence, conflict of interest, insider trading/front running, confidentiality, professional standard, compliance and responsibility of senior management.
hints: Correct - revenue maximisation is not a conduct principle and would conflict with independence.

questions.q: Research analysts must maintain records such as research reports, rationale for recommendations and client records for a minimum of:
questions.explanation: The RA Regulations require records to be maintained for at least five years, in physical or electronic form.

questions.q: SEBI has recognised which entity as the Research Analyst Administration and Supervisory Body (RAASB)?
questions.explanation: BSE Ltd was recognised by SEBI in 2024 as the RAASB; research analysts enlist with it and the deposit is marked as lien in its favour.
hints: AMFI is the mutual fund industry body.

questions.q: Which chart type plots only price changes and ignores the passage of time?
questions.explanation: Point and figure charts record X's (rises) and O's (falls) only when price moves by a set box size, so time is ignored.
hints: A line chart has time on the x-axis.
Candlesticks are plotted per time period.
Bar charts are plotted per time period.

questions.q: An uptrend is technically defined by a series of:
questions.explanation: An uptrend makes successively higher peaks and higher troughs; a downtrend makes lower highs and lower lows.
hints: That is a bearish volume signal.

questions.q: A double top pattern that is confirmed by a break below the intervening low is:
questions.explanation: A double top (an 'M' shape) forms after an uptrend; a close below the trough between the peaks confirms a bearish reversal.
hints: It is a reversal, and bearish.
Once confirmed it signals a trend change.
